key_insight: The paper argues that for autonomous scientific discovery, the main bottleneck is no longer agent prompting or workflows, but the design of the execution environment that shapes agent behavior.
engineering_relevance: For computational science systems, it reframes agent development as environment engineering: controlling permissions, artifacts, budgets, and human oversight to improve reliability, collaboration, and search efficiency.
method: Permissions engineering: bounded execution and isolated evaluation
Artifact engineering: filesystem and Git-based collaboration
Budget + human-in-the-loop engineering: cost-aware exploration and low-friction supervision
evidence_signal: EurekAgent reports new state-of-the-art results across multiple mathematics, kernel engineering, and machine learning tasks, including a 26-circle packing result achieved for under $11 in API cost.
watch_item: Environment controls can add implementation complexity and may still depend on careful tuning to avoid new failure modes or hidden constraints that bias agent behavior.
paper_title: EurekAgent: Agent Environment Engineering is All You Need For Autonomous Scientific Discovery
